systems.owner: Ministry of Education and Technical Education (MOETE)
systems.tiers: not stated; named only as the source of the data the student smart card integrates and of its data-privacy protocols; the paper does not say what EMIS does or who enters its data

systems.country_label: Smart Card; Student Digital Identity; Smart Student digital ID
systems.tiers: a per-student card integrating EMIS data: teacher assignments, test scores, digital attendance, school enrolment, digital course participation, biometrics, receipt of books and tablets, schools attended; as at 12 June 2025 developed but not yet received by students, first batch scheduled for mid-2025 in the pilot governorate of Suez, national rollout plan expected by October 2025; who enters the data is not stated

operational July 2024; real-time data from the Learning Management System on use of digital content by grade, gender, user type and location, with reports for each level of administration; said also to support student management, unified student profiles and academic performance tracking

systems.system: Learning Management System, Egyptian Knowledge Bank and digital and TV learning resources
systems.country_label: LMS; Egyptian Knowledge Bank; TV educational channels

systems.system: Tablet-based assessment management and delivery platform
systems.tiers: deployed July 2019; item banks, test administration and marking for grades 10-12, scores made available electronically to students, school principals, districts and directorates

note: No fact: the paper never says schools enter anything into EMIS or the smart card; it says only that the card draws per-student data (test scores, digital attendance, enrolment) from EMIS, so neither is classed. The parent may want this beside the other Egypt documents: the card was still a Suez pilot awaiting distribution on 12 June 2025, under a US$500 million IBRD loan.
